timed_text.text: You've got your baseline. You know where you're starting.
Who are you as a competitor?
Not what you want to achieve. Not what your stats say.
Athletes who compete from a clear sense of who they are outperform athletes who compete from outcome.
The difference between 'I want to win' and 'I am the kind of athlete who doesn't quit.'
Today you're going to write your identity. Present tense. Specific. Behavioral.
On your screen you're going to see a few examples. Then write two or three of your own.

steps.text: I am an athlete who shows up the same — whether I'm winning or losing.
I am an athlete who competes through discomfort.
I am an athlete who focuses on the next play, not the last one.
Now write 2–3 of your own. Present tense. Be specific. Who are you when you step onto the field?

timed_text.text: That's not a goal. That's a decision.
Every time you open this app from here on — that's who's showing up.
Go hit the journal. One question.

blocks.prompt: Which identity statement felt most powerful? Which one felt hardest to believe?
